2016.emphasis_summary: The board nominee skills matrix (workforce management, technology, multinational supply chain, finance and risk, public affairs) and nominee biographies fill the human_capital field, the CD&A summary stresses fiscal 2015 adjusted EPS of $4.69 and an after-tax ROIC of 13.9%, and the environment field describes the 5-percent-of-profit community giving pledge and the CSR report.
2016.notable_shifts: First available year in sample; no prior-year comparison.

2017.emphasis_summary: The skills matrix and nominee biographies repeat almost unchanged, but the environment_sustainability field is now a capital-allocation discussion (the balance between dividends and share repurchases, with Infrastructure & Investment Committee oversight), so the 2016 CSR-report material no longer appears there.
2017.notable_shifts: The finance-and-risk skill row drops the credit card servicing qualifier, and the environment field moves from CSR and community giving to dividend and repurchase philosophy, which is the main substantive change of the year. Net tone drops from 4.96 to 3.80.

2018.emphasis_summary: The human_capital field carries the same skills matrix, now with retail-industry, senior-leadership, real-estate, and workforce-management rows, while the environment field has little sustainability language (4 hits) and more compensation text (6 hits), and diversity_dei is empty.
2018.notable_shifts: Relative to 2017 the excerpts are almost unchanged, and net tone falls from 3.80 to 3.25 without a visible textual change.

2019.emphasis_summary: The human_capital field is a per-director summary of relevant skills, following the same skills-matrix structure as prior years, while the environment and compensation fields hold CD&A-style and governance text and diversity_dei is empty.
2019.notable_shifts: Excerpt content and net tone (3.25 in 2018, 3.25 in 2019) are essentially unchanged, so no company-level shift is identifiable beyond the repeated skills-matrix block.

2020.emphasis_summary: The human_capital field again leads with the skills matrix (workforce management, multinational operations, and supply chain logistics) and a statement that the company's reputation rests on guests, team members, communities, and shareholders, and this year's net tone (9.26) is the series high.
2020.notable_shifts: The excerpt text is almost identical to 2019, yet net tone jumps from 3.25 to 9.26, the largest year-over-year move in the series, so the change cannot be attributed to a visible textual shift and likely reflects the tone measure or the broader filing.

2021.emphasis_summary: The human_capital field includes a workforce diversity report commitment to increase representation of Black team members, and governance text on board refreshment (two new independent directors, Christine Leahy and Derica Rice, and a policy to rotate board leadership positions) runs alongside it.
2021.notable_shifts: Compared with 2020, the excerpts contain the first explicit diversity-goal language in the series (the Black team member representation commitment), and net tone falls from 9.26 back to 3.30, in line with the 2016-2019 baseline.

2022.emphasis_summary: Sustainability and ESG oversight is now written into the governance text (a Sustainability & ESG section describing Board and committee oversight), the compensation report is titled the Human Capital Management Committee Report, and the diversity_dei field carries 15 diversity hits alongside a governance practices table on board evaluations and refreshment.
2022.notable_shifts: Compared with 2021, the excerpts add explicit ESG and human-capital structure (a Governance & Sustainability Committee appears, and the compensation report is retitled), and environment-term hits in the environment field rise from 5 to 8; the 2016 and 2017 filings instead name the Human Resources and Compensation Committee.

2023.emphasis_summary: Human capital investment and DEI goals lead the human_capital field: a starting-wage range of $15 to $24 per hour, expanded health and retirement benefit eligibility, and progress on the 2022-2024 public Diversity, Equity & Inclusion goals, described as building a workforce that represents the communities Target serves.
2023.notable_shifts: Compared with 2022, the human_capital field gains explicit wage and benefit disclosures and a progress report on public DEI goals, and DEI keywords in human_capital rise from 14 to 17 hits. Net tone rises slightly from 3.51 to 3.63.

2024.emphasis_summary: Human capital is framed as a culture of caring, growing, and winning together and as a team that reflects the diverse communities and families Target serves, with board refreshment policies and the Lead Independent Director highlighted, and the compensation field is dense with workforce-related terms (35 hits).
2024.notable_shifts: Compared with 2023, DEI-term density in human_capital falls from 17 to 1 while the workforce framing and board-refreshment language take over, though the diversity_dei field stays at about 15 hits. Net tone rises from 3.63 to 4.30.
